questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body of mass $m$ is thrown with velocity u from the origin of a co-ordinate axes at an angle $\theta$ with the horizon. The magnitude of the angular momentum of the particle about the origin at time $\mathrm{t}$ when it is at the maximum height of the trajectory is proportional to
questions.solution: $\vec{L}=m u \cos \theta h_{\max }=m u \cos \theta \frac{u^2 \sin ^2 \theta}{2 g} \Rightarrow L=\frac{m u^3 \sin ^2 \theta \cos \theta}{2 g} \quad L \propto u^3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle is moving in $x-y$ plane according to $\vec{r}=b \cos \omega t \hat{i}+b \sin \omega t \hat{j}$. Where $\omega$ is constant. Which of the following statement(s) is / are true?
options: $\frac{E}{\omega}$ is a constant where $E$ is the total energy of the particle
The trajectory of the particle in $x-y$ plane is a circle
In $a_x-a_y$ plane, trajectory of the particle is an ellipse $\left(a_x, a_y\right.$ denotes the components of acceleration)
questions.solution:
$\vec{r}=b \cos \omega t i+b \sin \omega t j\vec{v}=\frac{d \vec{r}}{d t}=-b \omega \sin \omega t+b \omega \cos \omega t j(\vec{v})=\sqrt{b^2 \omega^2 \sin ^2 \omega t+b^2 \omega^2 \cos ^2 \omega t}(\vec{v})=b \omega \rightarrow$ constant $\quad \therefore E=\frac{1}{2} m v^2=$ constant
$E=\frac{1}{2} m\left[b^2 \omega^2\right] \quad \Rightarrow \frac{E}{\omega}=\frac{1}{2} m b^2 \cdot \omega=$ constant
$x=b \cos \omega ty=b \sin \omega tx^2+y^2=b^2 \rightarrow$ equation of circle
$\therefore \vec{a} \perp \vec{v} \quad$ So $\vec{a} \neq \omega^2 \vec{v}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A fighter plane, flying horizontally with a speed $360 \mathrm{kmph}$ at an altitude of $500 \mathrm{ m}$ drops a bomb for a target straight ahead of it on the ground. The bomb.should be dropped at what approximate distance ahead of the target ? Assume that acceleration due to gravity $(\mathrm{g})$ is $10 \mathrm{ ms}^{-2}$. Also neglect air drag
questions.solution: Hint: $v=360 \mathrm{ km} / \mathrm{h}=100 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}.\mathrm{h}=500 \mathrm{ m}\mathrm{R}=\mathrm{u} \sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{ h}}{\mathrm{ g}}}=100 \times \sqrt{\frac{2 \times 500}{10}}=1000 \mathrm{ m}$

questions.q: A projectile thrown with an initial velocity of $10 \mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ at an angle $\alpha$ with the horizontal. has a range of $5 \mathrm{m}$. Taking $g=10 \mathrm{ms}^{-2}$ and neglecting air resistance, what will he the estimated value of $\alpha$?
questions.solution:
Given, initial velocity of particle,

u=10 $\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$Range, $R=5 \mathrm{m}$ Gravitational acceleration,

g=10 $\mathrm{ms}^{-2}$As we known that, 
Range of projectile, $R=\frac{u^{2} \sin 2 \theta}{g}
or

\begin{aligned}$5 &=$\frac{(10)^{2} \sin 2 \alpha}{10}$\\
\sin 2 $\alpha$&=$\frac{5}{10}$\\
\sin 2 $\alpha$&=$\frac{1}{2}$\\
$\alpha$&=15^{{}^{\circ}} \\
$\left(90^{{}^{\circ}}-15^{{}^{\circ}}\right.&\left.=$75^{{}^{\circ}}\right)
\end{aligned}

questions.q: A simple pendulum of length $L$ swings in a vertical plane. The tension of the string when it makes an angle $\theta$ with the vertical and the bob of mass $m$ moves with a speed $v$ is $\mathrm{fg}$ is the gravitational acceleration)
questions.solution: The situation is given below For motion along a vertical circular track, the required centripetal force is along the radius and towards the centre of the circle is given by $T-m g \cos \theta=\frac{m v^{2}}{L}\Rightarrow \quad T=\frac{m v^{2}}{L}+m g \cos \theta$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Particle $A$ moves along $X$ -axis with a uniform velocity of magnitude $10 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$. Particle $B$ moves with uniform velocity $20 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$ along a direction making an angle of $60^{{}^{\circ}}$ with the positive direction of $X$ -axis as shown in the figure. The relative velocity of $B$ with respect to that of $A$ is
options: $10 \sqrt{5} \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$ along the bisection of the velocities of A and $B$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned}\text{$ The $component of velocity of } B \text{ along } x \text{ -direction }\\ &\begin{aligned} \mathbf{v}_{B x}&=20 \cos 60^{{}^{\circ}}=20 \times \frac{1}{2}=10 \mathrm{m}/ \mathrm{s}\\ \mathbf{v}_{A} \text{ and } =10 \hat{\mathbf{i}} \\ \mathbf{v}_{B} \text{ and } =10 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+10 \sqrt{3} \hat{\mathbf{j}}\\ \mathbf{v}_{B A} \text{ and } =\mathbf{v}_{B}-\mathbf{v}_{A}=10 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+10 \sqrt{3} \hat{\mathbf{j}}-10 \hat{\mathbf{i}}=10 \sqrt{3} \hat{\mathbf{j}} \end{aligned} \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A cricket ball thrown across a field is at heights $h_{1}$ and $h_{2}$ from the point of projection at times $t_{1}$ and $t_{2}$ respectively after the throw. The ball is caught by a fielder at the same height as that of projection. The time of flight of the ball in this journey is
questions.solution:
For vertically moment (for $\left.h_{1}\right)$
or
$\begin{array}{l}
h_{1}=u \sin \theta t_{1}-\frac{1}{2} g t_{1}^{2} \\
t_{1}=\frac{h_{1}+\frac{1}{2} g t_{1}^{2}}{u \sin \theta}
\end{array}$
$h_{2}=u \sin \theta t_{2}-\frac{1}{2} g t_{2}^{2}$
or $t_{2}=\frac{h_{2}+\frac{1}{2} g t_{2}^{2}}{u \sin \theta}$
Divide Eq. (i) by Eq. (ia)
$\begin{array}{l}
\frac{t_{1}}{t_{2}}=\frac{h_{1}+\frac{1}{2} g t_{1}^{2} / u \sin \theta}{h_{2}+\frac{1}{2} g t_{2}^{2} / u \sin \theta} \\
\Rightarrow h_{1} t_{2}-h_{2} t_{1}=\frac{g}{2}\left(t_{1} t_{2}^{2}-t_{1}^{2} t_{2}\right)
\end{array}$
The time of flight of the ball $T=\frac{2 u \sin \theta}{g}=\frac{2}{g}(u \sin \theta) \quad$ 
$=\frac{2}{g}\left[\frac{h_{1}+\frac{1}{2} g t_{1}^{2}}{t_{1}}\right]=\frac{2}{t_{1}}\left[\frac{h_{1}}{g}+\frac{t_{1}^{2}}{2}\right]$
$=\frac{h_{1}}{t_{1}} \times \frac{2}{g}+t_{1}=\frac{h_{1}}{t_{1}} \times\left(\frac{t_{1} t_{2}^{2}-t_{1}^{2} t_{2}}{h_{1} t_{2}-h_{2} t_{1}}\right)+t_{1}$
$=\frac{h_{1} t_{1} t_{2}^{2}-h_{1} t_{1}^{2} t_{2}+h_{1} t_{1}^{2} t_{2}-h_{2} t_{1}^{3}}{t_{1}\left(h_{1} t_{2}-h_{2} t_{1}\right)}$
$=\left(\frac{h_{1} t_{2}^{2}-h_{2} t_{1}^{2}}{h_{1} t_{2}-h_{2} t_{1}}\right)$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body is projected from the ground with a velocity $\mathbf{v}=(3 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+10 \hat{\mathbf{j}}) \mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}.$ The maximum height attained and the range of the body respectively are (given $g=10 \mathrm{ms}^{-2}$ )
questions.solution: (a) Given, $v=(3 i+10 j) m / s\Rightarrow \quad v_{x}=3$ and $v_{y}=10\therefore$ Maximum height attained, $H=\frac{v_y^{2}}{2 g} \begin{aligned}&=\frac{10 \times 10}{2 \times 10}=5 \mathrm{m}\\ \text{ Range }= v_{x} \times T=V_{x} \times \frac{2 v_{y}}{g}&=\frac{3 \times 2 \times 10}{10}=6 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle is projected from the ground with a kinetic energy $E$ at an angle of $60^{{}^{\circ}}$ with the horizontal. Its kinetic energy at the highest point of its motion will be
questions.solution: At ground, $E=\frac{1}{2} m u^{2}$ At highest point, $E^{\prime}=\frac{1}{2} m\left(u \cos 60^{{}^{\circ}}\right)^{2}$ E^{\prime}=$\frac{E}{4}$

questions.q: From the top of a tower, $80 \mathrm{m}$ high from the ground, a stone is thrown in the horizontal direction with a velocity of $8 \mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$. The stone reaches the ground after a time $t^{\prime}$ and falls at a distance of " $\mathrm{d}$ ' from the foot of the tower. Assuming $g=10 \mathrm{m} / \mathrms^{2}$, the time $t$ and distance d are given respectively by
questions.solution: Given, $h=80 \mathrm{m}, v=8 \mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ and $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{ms}^{-2}$ Here, $\begin{aligned} h &=\frac{1}{2} g t^{2} \\ 80 &=\frac{1}{2} \times10 \times t^{2} \\ t &=4 \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}$ and $\quad x=v t=8 \times 4=32 \mathrm{m}$
